simple.meaning: גְּבֶרֶת (gᵉbereth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “mistress.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 16:4. The surrounding context includes prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּבֶרֶת (H1404) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: גְּבֶרֶת (gᵉbereth) / H1404 is traced through Genesis 16:4, Genesis 16:8, Genesis 16:9, 2 Kings 5:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.

timeline.evidenceText: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where did you come from? Where are you going?”
Yahweh’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.”
She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”
Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master,
for an unloved woman when she is married,

It will be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the creditor, so with the debtor; as with the taker of interest, so with the giver of interest.
“Sit in silence, and go into darkness,
You said, ‘I will be a princess forever,’
